title: Net Revenue Retention (NRR) and Negative Churn

parts.visual:
A startup has 100 customers paying $100 a month. Over the year, 10 customers cancel (churn), losing $1,000. However, the 90 remaining customers love the product so much they upgrade their accounts, generating $3,000 in *new* revenue. Even though the startup lost customers, their total revenue *increased*.

The Math of Expansion:
1. NRR (Net Revenue Retention): The percentage of revenue retained from existing customers, including both cancellations (downgrades) and upgrades (upsells).
2. Negative Churn: The magical state where NRR is over 100%. It means the revenue from your existing customer base is growing automatically, even if you never sign a single new customer.
parts.audio: In modern SaaS, Net Revenue Retention is the single most important metric. An NRR of 120% means your company grows 20% every year automatically. It is the closest thing to financial anti-gravity in the business world.

questions.question: A startup has an NRR of 80%. What does this mathematically mean for their future?
options: They are bleeding to death. It means every year, their existing customer base shrinks by 20% in value. The startup must spend massive amounts of money acquiring new customers just to replace the revenue they are actively losing.
questions.correct_answer: They are bleeding to death. It means every year, their existing customer base shrinks by 20% in value. The startup must spend massive amounts of money acquiring new customers just to replace the revenue they are actively losing.
questions.explanation: You cannot outrun a leaky bucket.

questions.question: Listen to the CEO explaining their pricing model to achieve Negative Churn. What is the tactic?
questions.tts_text: We don't charge a flat fee. We charge 'per user'. When a small company signs up, they pay $50 for 5 employees. But when that company grows and hires 50 more employees, our software automatically bills them $500. We grow as they grow.
options: Value Metric Pricing. By tying the price directly to the customer's usage (per user, per gigabyte, per transaction), the startup guarantees automatic revenue expansion without the sales team having to 're-sell' the product.
questions.correct_answer: Value Metric Pricing. By tying the price directly to the customer's usage (per user, per gigabyte, per transaction), the startup guarantees automatic revenue expansion without the sales team having to 're-sell' the product.
questions.explanation: If your customers are successful, you get an automatic raise.

questions.question: What is the difference between 'Gross Retention' and 'Net Revenue Retention'?
options: Gross Retention only measures the revenue you kept (maximum 100%), completely ignoring upgrades. Net Revenue Retention (NRR) includes the upgrades and upsells, which allows the number to go above 100% into the magical 'Negative Churn' zone.
questions.correct_answer: Gross Retention only measures the revenue you kept (maximum 100%), completely ignoring upgrades. Net Revenue Retention (NRR) includes the upgrades and upsells, which allows the number to go above 100% into the magical 'Negative Churn' zone.
questions.explanation: Gross retention tells you if the product is broken. NRR tells you if the business is scalable.

questions.question: Why do VCs value a company with 130% NRR significantly higher than a company with 95% NRR, even if both have the same total revenue today?
options: Because of Compound Interest. The company with 130% NRR is an unstoppable snowball rolling down a hill; its revenue will compound exponentially without massive marketing spend. The 95% company will eventually stall out and die.
questions.correct_answer: Because of Compound Interest. The company with 130% NRR is an unstoppable snowball rolling down a hill; its revenue will compound exponentially without massive marketing spend. The 95% company will eventually stall out and die.
questions.explanation: NRR is the ultimate predictor of future exponential growth.

questions.question: Order the words to describe the magic of SaaS:
questions.explanation: When your existing customers fuel your growth automatically.
